## Related Posts

- [The Inference Shift](/posts/20260511-the-inference-shift/): the architectural half of the cost question, arguing that agentic inference is a different workload from answer inference and needs a memory-hierarchy-first machine to get cheap.
- [The Math Behind the Cost of AI Agents](/posts/20260513-the-math-behind-the-cost-of-ai-agents/): why per-token price cuts don't automatically make agents cheap, since agent token consumption grows quadratically without caching.
- [Sam Altman on Compute, AGI, and Human Agency](/posts/20260730-altman-compute-agi-human-agency/): the build-out argued from inside one of the buyers, on the premise that demand for intelligence is effectively uncapped.
- [The 2028 Global Intelligence Crisis: Scenario and Rebuttal](/posts/20260502-2028-intelligence-crisis/): a scenario writer and a rebutting trading firm read the same 2028 horizon this chip curve runs out to, and disagree on what it means.
- [Anthropic Economic Index](/posts/20260423-anthropic-economic-index/): measurement on the consumption side, tracking where the intelligence being bought actually gets used.
